page: Amazon Web Services g5g.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 32 dedicated arm64 physical cores based on the AWS Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core. Memory provision stands at 64.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU alongside an L3 cache configuration of 32 MB. Hardware acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA T4G GPU offering 16 GB of VRAM. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps, while integrated local storage is absent, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark analysis reflects the instance's strengths in multi-threaded computation alongside entry-level GPU processing capabilities. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieves average-tier results, generating 48574.86 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 11551.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Software compilation through Clang and ray tracing tests show steady throughput. Single-threaded performance displays lower execution capability, with a Geekbench single-core mark of 952.0 and lower quartile rankings in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In inference tests, the platform demonstrates prompt processing rates of 441.91 tokens per second on 135M models and text generation speeds of 15.24 tokens per second on 7B models.

The coupling of power-efficient ARM architecture with an NVIDIA T4G GPU offers qualitative operational efficiency for graphics and inference workloads compared to legacy x86 configurations. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural consideration for network storage latency and throughput. The system is suited for arm64-native Android game streaming, video encoding pipelines, lightweight machine learning inference, and distributed graphics rendering tasks.
